terms.meaning: A six-character code such as a color written in hexadecimal digits.
A lighter version of a color made by adding transparency.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Core status and neutral colors
sections.what: Holds the green, amber, red, and accent colors, plus the background, border, and text tones used by charts and maps.
sections.why: Charts and maps cannot read the theme's named colors, so they use these matching values.
sections.watch_out: These must match the stylesheet values by hand.

sections.name: REGION_PALETTE
sections.title: Region colors for the scan chart
sections.what: Assigns one color to each world region used on the benchmark bubble chart.
sections.why: The comment says region colors are fixed by the master design.
sections.watch_out: Unknown is included so that unexpected regions still get a color.

sections.name: HOUSE_REGION_PALETTE
sections.title: House region colors for scan slides
sections.what: Assigns colors to the house-specific regions, which split the Middle East and Africa.
sections.why: The house deck uses its own region grouping.
sections.watch_out: Asia-Pacific reuses the Asia color from the main region palette, so changing that one changes both.

sections.name: HOUSE_CATEGORICAL
sections.title: Ordered color list for categories
sections.what: Lists the house colors in a fixed order so charts with many categories can each get a distinct color.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code, beyond the comment that it avoids running out of hues.
sections.watch_out: The order matters, so reordering the list changes which category gets which color.

summary: Holds the fixed color codes used by charts, maps, and diagrams that cannot read the theme's named colors.
purpose: Provides one place for JavaScript-drawn colors, so charts and the theme match.
why: The comment says these must mirror the theme in the stylesheet, because some drawing tools need plain color codes.
how: Defines the status, accent, neutral, and grey colors as plain codes, then builds lighter tints from the status colors. It also defines a region palette for the scan bubble chart and a separate house palette for scan slides.
inputs: None at runtime. The values are fixed.
outputs: Named color constants used by chart and slide code.
risks: Editing a color here without changing the stylesheet makes charts and the theme disagree.
debug: If a chart color differs from the page, compare the constant here with the matching variable in the stylesheet.
